title: Tommy Flanagan's first night with Ella
summary: Ella turned on a nervous Flanagan, Gus told her off, and Flanagan became her best accompanist; the previous pianist was Don Abney.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Just like when Tommy Flanagan, for instance, got with the group. Well, we were playing some club in Cleveland, and -- I think it was the Harlem Club in Cleveland. And this was his first night with the group.
Yeah.
And he was doing the best he could, and she turned around on him and liked to scare him to death. And so I -- I saw it and I just said, 'Turn around,' just like that.
At her?
I sure did.
Good for you.
And, boy, that kind of shocked her, I believe, in a way.
Yeah.
But she got over it. I walked behind her, waiting for her to say, 'You're fired,' one of those things.
But she didn't, and I told her, I said, 'This is his first night and he's nervous and he doesn't know the numbers right then.' The first time he ever played behind her, you know.
Yeah. No rehearsal or anything?
Well, we had a rehearsal, but --
But it's not the same --
It was just right then and there.
Yeah, right.
When he came in, you see.
Yeah, right.
And he did good, you know. But she was uptight, too, you know, at that. Losing her piano player, we called him Lloyd Proper at times, because he talks proper. You know him.
Not Lloyd.
No, his name is not Lloyd.
No, no, I know, but I was thinking --
Not Lou Levy. No, this is a black guy.
Kind of got big eyes.
Not Milton Larkin.
Not Milton Larkin.
I don't mean Milt Larkin. I mean Ellis Larkin.
No, no, no, not Ellis. I'll tell you a little later.
(Don Abney)
It'll come. We'll go back to it.
So --
Well, come to find out Tommy accompanied her better than anyone, didn't he?
That's right. He stayed with her. He's still with her, when she goes out.
Yeah, yeah. And she is a person that really appreciates an accompanist.
Oh, yes, she does.
That does half her work for her, or a whole lot of her work --
I loved working with Ella, I really did.
